scenes.title: Where and when
narration: St. Louis Shag originated in St. Louis, Missouri, in the 1930s.
It evolved from a combination of Lindy Hop, Collegiate Shag, and Charleston.
The dance has maintained its characteristics through shifts in musical styles, including the transition from swing to rock and roll, jump blues, and R&B.

narration: Today it is a living tradition.

scenes.title: Watch it
narration: The dance is performed in a closed position with a stationary 8-count basic.

Common variations include the triple-step, kick, triple-step, kick pattern; the Kenny Wetzel version (triple-step, kick, step-stomp, run-run); and the Eddie Plunkett and Dottie Spokesfield version (triple-step, kick, double kick).
Dancers often incorporate inside crosses, fall off the logs, and various stomps, kicks, and taps.
Watch for Inside crosses, Fall off the logs.

The music is characterized by strong, driving rhythms that support the percussive nature of the footwork.
